Title: Reject canceled->delivered (terminal state protection)

ExpectedResult: 400; canceled is terminal and must NOT transition to delivered; status remains canceled

Title: Regular user token cannot update another user's order (SEC-03 role enforcement)
Precondition: One admin-owned order and a regular user token
TestData: User A token on an order owned by another user (or admin-created)
ExpectedResult: 403; no mutation - a non-admin JWT (role=user) must be rejected before any order update, regardless of who owns the order
HumanReview: STUDENT-ADDED (case AI missed). AI's API3-011/013 tested 'user token' generically but did not make the SEC-03 role check explicit against an order the user does not own. BUG (verified): authenticateToken never checks role=admin, so a user token updates any order (200). Reason AI missed: model limitation - the AI assumed role enforcement existed rather than verifying the middleware only checks token validity.

Title: Read-back verifies persisted status after a successful update

ExpectedResult: The read-back shows status=confirmed for the target order and unchanged statuses for all other orders
HumanReview: STUDENT-ADDED (case AI missed). AI asserted success/persistence only in the oracle text and never added a GET read-back verification step. Reason AI missed: state-transition modeling was incomplete - the AI did not include the verification action to confirm the persisted state and isolate scope.

Title: Repeated transition (confirmed->confirmed) is rejected (documented non-idempotent behavior)

Reason AI missed: prompt quality - the AI did not model re-transition/idempotency semantics for the state machine.
